question: What has changed at Merrill since the start of the year?
reasoning_content:

cells.label: fact

items.text: Merrill created two new kinds of fees for third-party asset managers: a data analytics fee and a negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee,' effective January 1, 2027.
items.quote: Two kinds of fees have been newly created. Third-party managers can buy as much as $1.4 million worth of "incentives" per annum through one fee, by maxing out data analytics buys. The second fee is a basis points revenue share that can cost asset managers as much as 0.1% on all Merill assets they manage. ... the Bank of America subsidiary is making it possible to pay more to get more visibility and middleman love, effective, Jan. 1, 2027.

items.text: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per firm per year for data on actively managed products, and between $25,000 and $550,000 for data on passive ETFs.
items.quote: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios. Data on passive ETFs managed through Merrill's platforms will cost between $25,000 and $550,000.

items.text: Merrill's new negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee' will cost up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% to a maximum of 0.1%.
items.quote: Its new "negotiable" revenue-sharing "support fee" will cost up to $1 million, for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% on high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth assets, to a maximum 0.1% on third party mutual funds, money market funds, and active ETFs.

items.text: Merrill launched two new services, Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), to help clients implement tax-efficient transitions and systematic cash deployment within personalized investment strategies.
items.quote: Merrill today announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services that combine automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment into managed or custom managed investment strategies in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program (IAP).

items.text: Merrill has returned to veteran broker recruiting, having largely pulled back from it at the end of 2017, with recruited assets to the wealth unit doubling year-over-year as of October.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: Merrill executives said the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities, and Merrill's president and co-head noted client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter.
items.quote: While the Merrill executive did not mention new AI tools, the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities. ... At Merrill Lynch, client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter, said Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management.

cells.reason: Passages describe new initiatives (data/support fees, TET/DCA services), a strategic change (return to veteran broker recruiting), and continued investment in AI/digital and alternatives, all within 2026.
